summary: An excellent preliminary report. Your reef-monitoring mission concept is well justified with quantified objectives tied to named users, your Gantt plan is robust with contingencies, and your orbit hand calculations are correct and interpreted against your objectives. Presentation is professional. To reach the very top of the rubric, address latitude dependence in your coverage analysis and add a requirements table.
next_steps: In Preliminary Progress, note that your 24.2° equatorial track shift overstates spacing at the reef's latitude (~18–20°S), where ground-track spacing is smaller — discuss how this changes your weekly-coverage conclusion and consider computing spacing at 18°S.
Add a table of mission requirements (derived from your four objectives) with a brief note on how each will be verified, to close the gap between objectives and requirements in C1.
Briefly flag the feasibility of 10 m GSD at 600 km (aperture/telescope sizing) as a design question to resolve in the full assignment, so the swath trade is framed early.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your mission goal is clear, your four objectives are quantified, and users (GBRMPA, AIMS, CSIRO, BoM) are explicitly tied to their needs, supported by references [1]–[6]. To fully reach the top of the Accomplished band, add an explicit requirements table with verification approach linking objectives to mission requirements.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your Gantt chart (Figure 1) is well structured with task logic tied to the mission (orbit before comms), a risk/contingency table (Table 1), float, and a planned-sources table (Table 2) including SMAD and lecture notes. This is a robust, mission-aligned plan; little is missing at this level.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Your hand calculations (a=6978 km, T=5801 s, 14.9 orbits/day, i≈97.8° SSO, 24.2° track shift) are correct and interpreted against your objectives, with a swath trade identified and STK setup completed. Strengthen the coverage analysis by accounting for latitude dependence at the reef, and note the aperture implications of 10 m GSD at 600 km.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Your report has a logical structure, clear writing, labelled figures and tables with explained legends, and consistent IEEE-style citations matching the reference list. Presentation is professional; maintain this standard in the full report.
